extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents) handling Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs) for design applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, filing, and processing Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) for design patent applications, including signature, filing-date, fee, inventorship, and notice rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA must be properly signed (see 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)(v) and 37 CFR 1.33(b)). In a joint application with no attorney or agent, all applicants must sign the CPA request in order for the CPA request to be considered properly signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned or improperly signed CPA request will be placed in the file of the prior application and is entitled to an application filing date, but is ineffective to abandon the prior application. A CPA will NOT be examined until the CPA request is properly signed. A request for a CPA may be signed by a registered practitioner acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34. A request for a CPA may also be signed by the assignee(s) of the entire interest if accompanied by papers establishing the assignee's ownership under 37 CFR 3.73(b), unless such papers were filed in the prior application and ownership has not changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address for CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence concerning the CPA will be sent by the Office to the correspondence address as it appears in the prior nonprovisional application until a new power of attorney, or change of correspondence address signed by an attorney or agent of record in the prior application, is filed in the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should file a new power of attorney or signed change of correspondence address if they want correspondence for the CPA sent to a different address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date must be on separate paper
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a CPA is the date on which a request on a separate paper for a CPA is filed. A request for a CPA cannot be submitted as a part of papers filed for another purpose, see 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'separate paper' requirement is intended to preclude burying a CPA request in a paper submitted primarily for another purpose (e.g., within an amendment after final). If a paper filed in the prior application contains a CPA request but not on a separate paper, the request is ineffective; the examiner should contact applicant or notify applicant in the next Office action (form paragraph 2.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized methods of filing and facsimile receipt rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper requesting a CPA may be sent by mail, by facsimile transmission, or filed directly at the Customer Service Window. The date of receipt accorded to a CPA request sent by facsimile transmission is the date the complete transmission is received by an Office facsimile unit, unless the transmission is completed on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, in which case receipt is the next succeeding non-holiday weekday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants filing by facsimile may include PTO/SB/29A 'Receipt for Facsimile Transmitted CPA' containing identifying info; USPTO will separate, date-stamp, verify identifying info, and mail the receipt back. The PTO will not verify whether the CPA was accompanied by other papers; the receipt cannot acknowledge papers other than the CPA request. Applicants are cautioned not to include information intended for retention in the application file on the receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile filing of fees is not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant filing a CPA by facsimile transmission does not include an authorization to charge the basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee to a deposit account or to a credit card using PTO-2038, the application will be treated under 37 CFR 1.53(f) as having been filed without the appropriate fees (as fees cannot otherwise be transmitted by facsimile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing by fax, include PTO-2038 authorization or be prepared for the CPA to be treated as filed without fees and for the resulting procedures (notification, time to pay, surcharge) to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of transmission when Office has no evidence of facsimile receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.6(f) requires that a showing thereunder include, inter alia, a copy of the sending unit’s report confirming transmission of the application or evidence that came into being after the complete transmission of the application and within one business day of the complete transmission of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of a faxed CPA, provide the sending unit's transmission report or other near-term corroborating evidence to establish transmission under 1.6(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing does not apply to CPA filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificate of Mailing Procedure under 37 CFR 1.8 does not apply to filing a request for a CPA, since the filing of such a request is considered to be a filing of national application papers for the purpose of obtaining an application filing date (37 CFR 1.8(a)(2)(i)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on a certificate of mailing to preserve CPA filing date in abandonment scenarios; the MPEP gives examples where certificate-of-mailing dates do not prevent abandonment of the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees and surcharge requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing fees for a CPA are the basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(b)(1)), the search fee (37 CFR 1.16(l)), and the examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(p)). See 37 CFR 1.53(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general authorization to charge fees to a deposit account filed in the prior application carries over to the CPA. If a filing date has been assigned but fees are insufficient or omitted, applicant will be notified and given time (usually 2 months, subject to 37 CFR 1.136(a)) to file missing fees and pay surcharge per 37 CFR 1.16(f) to prevent abandonment. For CPAs filed on/after July 1, 2005, surcharge under 1.16(f) is required if any required fee is paid after the CPA filing date. A CPA will not be placed upon the files for examination until all required parts, including any surcharge, are received; it is inappropriate to conduct interviews or issue actions on the merits before required fees/surcharge are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity status must be reasserted
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity status established in the parent application does not automatically carry over to a CPA. Status as a small entity must be specifically established in every application in which the status is available and desired. 37 CFR 1.27(c)(4) provides that the refiling of an application as a continued prosecution application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) requires a new assertion of continued entitlement to small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the request for a CPA specifically indicates that the filing fee is to be charged in the small entity amount or otherwise includes an assertion of entitlement to small entity status, the large entity filing fee should be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and continuity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior application and the CPA, the petition for extension of time should be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application. The 'separate paper' requirement of 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2) is intended to preclude burying a CPA request in a paper submitted primarily for another purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CPA is not improper simply because the request is combined with a petition for extension of time. While the filing of a CPA is not strictly a reply to an Office action, it is a paper directed to the prior application and will be considered a 'reply' for purposes of 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3). An authorization in the prior application to charge required fees or extension fees to a deposit account or credit card will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in the prior application for establishing continuity. If an extension of time directed to the prior application is filed as a separate paper, it must be accompanied by its own certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 (or 1.10 for Express Mail) if those benefits are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to applicant that CPA established
rubrics_metrics.description: Since a 'Notice of Abandonment' is not mailed in the prior application as a result of the filing of a CPA nor is a filing receipt normally mailed for a CPA, the examiner should advise the applicant that a request for a CPA has been granted by including form paragraph 2.30 in the first Office action of the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.30 in the first Office action of a CPA to advise applicant that a request for a CPA is acceptable and that a CPA has been established. If the CPA was treated as an RCE (improper), use the appropriate RCE form paragraph instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional CPA requests are treated as unconditional
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'conditional' request for a CPA will not be permitted. Any 'conditional' request for a CPA submitted as a separate paper with an amendment after final in an application will be treated as an unconditional request for a CPA of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treating a conditional request as unconditional will result in abandonment of the prior application and (if so instructed) the amendment after final will be treated as a preliminary amendment in the CPA. The examiner should advise the applicant that a 'conditional' request has been treated as unconditional by including form paragraph 2.35 in the first Office action of the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineffective CPA requests not on separate paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner recognizes that a paper filed in the prior application contains a request for a CPA, but the request is not in a separate paper, the examiner should, if possible, contact applicant by telephone to notify applicant that the request for a CPA is ineffective or notify the applicant in the next Office action that the CPA request is ineffective by using form paragraph 2.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.31 to inform applicant that the request for a CPA is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2) and no CPA has been established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship carries over unless properly changed
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventive entity set forth in the prior nonprovisional application automatically carries over into the CPA UNLESS the request for a CPA is accompanied by or includes on filing a statement requesting the deletion of the name(s) of the person(s) who are not inventors of the invention being claimed in the CPA. 37 CFR 1.53(d)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement requesting deletion must be signed by person(s) authorized pursuant to 37 CFR 1.33(b). The examiner should acknowledge such a deletion request in the first Office action using form paragraph 2.32. A new oath or declaration naming an inventor not named in the prior application does not change the inventive entity; to add an inventor or otherwise correct inventorship the applicant must file a request under 37 CFR 1.48 with the required fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)). Failure to file the proper 1.48 request may result in rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(f). Use form paragraph 2.33 where a CPA identifies a new inventor without a proper 1.48 request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of earlier filing date; specific reference rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA is a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120 to every application assigned the application number identified in the request; 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2) provides that a request for a CPA is the specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120 to the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further amendment to the specification of the CPA nor a reference in the CPA’s application data sheet is required by 35 U.S.C. 120 or 37 CFR 1.78(a) to identify or reference the prior application. Where an application claims a benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 of a chain of applications, the application must reference the first (earliest) application and every intermediate application. In a chain of CPAs, each CPA by operation of 37 CFR 1.53(d)(7) contains the required specific reference to its immediate prior application and every other application assigned that application number. Any amendment to the specification or ADS attempting to add such a reference will not be entered; use form paragraph 2.34 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer carryover
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed in the parent application carries over to a CPA because the CPA retains the same application number as the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not want the terminal disclaimer to carry over to the CPA, applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 along with the required petition fee requesting the terminal disclaimer not be carried over. See MPEP § 1490 for withdrawing a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior restriction election carryover conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An election made in the prior application carries over to the CPA only if all of the following conditions are met: (A) the CPA is designated as a continuation or is not designated at all (i.e., the CPA is NOT designated as a divisional); (B) there was an express election by the applicant in reply to a restriction requirement in the prior application; (C) the CPA presents claim(s) drawn only to invention(s) claimed in the prior application; and (D) the CPA does not contain an indication that a shift in election is desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where all conditions are met, the examiner’s first action should repeat the restriction requirement made in the prior application to the extent still applicable and include a statement that prosecution is being continued on the invention elected and prosecuted by applicant in the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) and preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All IDSs filed in the prior application that comply with 37 CFR 1.98 will be considered in a CPA by the examiner; IDSs filed before the mailing of a first Office action on the merits will be considered regardless of prior prosecution events. Applicants are encouraged to file IDSs and preliminary amendments at the time of filing the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an IDS after the first Office action is mailed could delay prosecution; preliminary amendments filed after the CPA filing date could be denied under 37 CFR 1.115 if they unduly interfere with preparation of the first Office action. If applicant needs more time to prepare a preliminary amendment or IDS, applicant can request a three-month suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(b) at the time of filing the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of affidavits and declarations carry over
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits and declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131 and 1.132) filed during the prosecution of the parent nonprovisional application automatically become part of the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No copy of the original affidavit or declaration filed in the parent application need be filed in the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access waiver and pending status
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is construed to include a waiver of confidentiality by the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent that any member of the public entitled under 37 CFR 1.14 to obtain access to, copies of, or information concerning either the prior application or any continuing application may be given similar access to the other application(s) in the file. However, all applications in the file jacket of a pending CPA are treated as pending, rather than abandoned, in determining whether copies of, and access to, such applications will be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should be aware that filing a CPA may open access to prior application material for those entitled to access under 37 CFR 1.14; see MPEP § 103 and IFW guidance for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy of CPA chain
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of a CPA will be prepared by the Certification Branch upon request. The certified copy will consist of a copy of the most recent non-continued prosecution application in the chain of CPAs. The filing date of the CPA will be shown in the certified copy as the filing date of the most recent non-continued prosecution application in the chain of CPAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Certification Branch procedures to obtain certified copies; the certified copy reflects the most recent non-continued prosecution application's filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTO forms for CPA filings and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/29 (Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) Request Transmittal) and PTO/SB/29A (Receipt For Facsimile Transmitted CPA) may be used by applicant for filing a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d). The TCs use various notice forms (e.g., PTO-2011, PTO-2012, PTO-2021, PTO-2018, PTO-2019) to notify applicants of defects regarding CPA filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/29 is for design applications only and notes filing qualifications (prior application must be a design application complete per 37 CFR 1.51(b)), that C-I-P is not permitted as a CPA, that filing the CPA expressly abandons the prior application, and other warnings (e.g., credit card info not to be included on the form). Use the listed TC notice forms for defect/missing parts/abandonment communications.
